Adaptive rejection \",\n        \"sampling requires a log-concave density.\",\n        absc[i], absc[i + 1], z[i]), call. = FALSE)\n    }","newString":"    if (z[i] < absc[i] - tol || z[i] > absc[i + 1] + tol) {\n      stop(sprintf(paste0(\n        \"Non-log-concave density detected: tangent lines at x = %.6g and \",\n        \"x = %.6g intersect out of order (z = %.6g). Adaptive rejection \",\n        \"sampling requires a log-concave density.\"),\n        absc[i], absc[i + 1], z[i]), call. = FALSE)\n    }","originalFile":"# ==============================================================================\n# ars.R -- Adaptive Rejection Sampling (Gilks & Wild, 1992)\n#\n# Public API:\n#   ars(n, f, domain = c(-Inf, Inf), x_init = NULL, ...)  -- draw n samples\n#   test()                                                 -- run test suite\n#\n# The implementation is split into small, single-purpose helper functions\n# (prefixed with \".\") that mirror the structure of the Gilks & Wild algorithm:\n# building the piecewise-linear upper/lower hulls, sampling from the upper\n# hull, performing the squeeze/rejection tests, and updating the hull with\n# newly evaluated points. All helpers are pure functions of their arguments\n# (no shared mutable state), which keeps them independently testable.\n# ==============================================================================\n\n## -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n## 1. Input validation\n## -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#' Validate the arguments to ars() before any sampling work begins.\n.validate_ars_inputs <- function(n, f, domain, x_init) {\n  if (!is.function(f)) {\n    stop(\"`f` must be a function that evaluates the (possibly unnormalized) \",\n         \"density, e.g. dnorm.\", call. = FALSE)\n  }\n  if (!is.numeric(n) || length(n) != 1 || is.na(n) || n <= 0 ||\n      n != round(n)) {\n    stop(\"`n` must be a single positive integer (number of samples).\",\n         call. = FALSE)\n  }\n  if (!is.numeric(domain) || length(domain) != 2 || any(is.na(domain))) {\n    stop(\"`domain` must be a numeric vector of length 2: c(lower, upper).\",\n         call. = FALSE)\n  }\n  if (domain[1] >= domain[2]) {\n    stop(\"`domain` lower bound must be strictly less than the upper bound.\",\n         call. = FALSE)\n  }\n  if (!is.null(x_init)) {\n    if (!is.numeric(x_init) || length(x_init) < 2 || any(is.na(x_init))) {\n      stop(\"`x_init` must be a numeric vector with at least 2 finite values.\",\n           call. = FALSE)\n    }\n    if (any(x_init <= domain[1]) || any(x_init >= domain[2])) {\n      stop(\"All `x_init` points must lie strictly inside `domain`.\",\n           call. = FALSE)\n    }\n  }\n\n  # Sanity-check that f behaves like a density: non-negative, finite, and\n  # not identically zero on a handful of probe points inside the domain.\n  probe <- .probe_points(domain, x_init)\n  vals <- suppressWarnings(f(probe))\n  if (!is.numeric(vals) || length(vals) != length(probe)) {\n    stop(\"`f` must be vectorized: given a numeric vector it must return a \",\n         \"numeric vector of the same length.\", call. = FALSE)\n  }\n  if (any(is.na(vals)) || any(vals < 0)) {\n    stop(\"`f` returned NA or negative values; it must be a valid \",\n         \"(possibly unnormalized) density.\", call. = FALSE)\n  }\n  if (all(vals == 0)) {\n    stop(\"`f` evaluates to 0 everywhere it was probed inside `domain`; \",\n         \"check that `domain` matches the support of the density.\",\n         call. = FALSE)\n  }\n  invisible(TRUE)\n}\n\n#' A handful of points inside `domain` used to sanity-check `f`.\n.probe_points <- function(domain, x_init) {\n  a <- domain[1]; b <- domain[2]\n  if (!is.null(x_init)) return(x_init)\n  if (is.finite(a) && is.finite(b)) {\n    a + (b - a) * c(0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9)\n  } else if (is.finite(a)) {\n    a + c(0.5, 1, 2, 5)\n  } else if (is.finite(b)) {\n    b - c(0.5, 1, 2, 5)\n  } else {\n    c(-5, -1, 0, 1, 5)\n  }\n}\n\n## -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n## 2. Log-density and numerical derivative\n## -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#' Build a (possibly unnormalized) log-density function from f, clamped to\n#' `domain` so that log(0) outside the support does not propagate as NaN.\n.make_log_density <- function(f, domain) {\n  function(x) {\n    val <- rep(-Inf, length(x))\n    inside <- x > domain[1] & x < domain[2]\n    if (any(inside)) {\n      fx <- f(x[inside])\n      val[inside] <- log(fx)\n    }\n    val\n  }\n}\n\n#' Central-difference numerical derivative of `logf`, clamped to stay\n#' strictly inside `domain` so evaluation never lands outside the support.\n.make_log_density_derivative <- function(logf, domain) {\n  function(x) {\n    eps <- pmax(1e-6, abs(x) * 1e-5)\n    lo <- pmax(x - eps, domain[1] + 1e-10)\n    hi <- pmin(x + eps, domain[2] - 1e-10)\n    h <- pmax(hi - lo, 1e-12)\n    (logf(hi) - logf(lo)) / h\n  }\n}\n\n## -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n## 3. Choosing starting abscissae\n## -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#' Expand `x` outward (in the given direction) until `hprime` has the sign\n#' required for the tail to be integrable, or until the finite domain bound\n#' is reached (in which case no sign condition is required).\n.expand_to_valid_tail <- function(x, hprime, bound, direction, min_slope,\n                                   max_iter = 60) {\n  step <- max(1, abs(x))\n  for (i in seq_len(max_iter)) {\n    slope <- hprime(x)\n    ok <- if (direction > 0) slope <= -min_slope else slope >= min_slope\n    if (ok) return(x)\n    x_next <- x + direction * step\n    if (direction > 0 && x_next >= bound) {\n      if (is.finite(bound)) return(bound - 1e-6 * max(1, abs(bound)))\n    }\n    if (direction < 0 && x_next <= bound) {\n      if (is.finite(bound)) return(bound + 1e-6 * max(1, abs(bound)))\n    }\n    x <- x_next\n    step <- step * 2\n  }\n  stop(\"Could not find a starting point with the required tail behavior \",\n       \"(h'(x) must eventually change sign away from the mode). This \",\n       \"usually means the density is not log-concave, or its tails decay \",\n       \"too slowly.\", call. = FALSE)\n}\n\n#' Choose initial abscissae satisfying the ARS boundary requirements:\n#' h'(x1) > 0 if the domain is unbounded below, h'(xk) < 0 if unbounded\n#' above. Interior guesses are used as-is (and refined by later hull\n#' updates during sampling).\n.initialize_abscissae <- function(hprime, domain, x_init, min_slope = 1e-8) {\n  a <- domain[1]; b <- domain[2]\n\n  if (!is.null(x_init)) {\n    pts <- sort(unique(x_init))\n  } else if (is.finite(a) && is.finite(b)) {\n    pts <- a + (b - a) * c(0.25, 0.75)\n  } else if (is.finite(a)) {\n    pts <- a + c(0.5, 2)\n  } else if (is.finite(b)) {\n    pts <- b - c(2, 0.5)\n  } else {\n    pts <- c(-1, 1)\n  }\n\n  if (!is.finite(a)) {\n    pts[1] <- .expand_to_valid_tail(pts[1], hprime, a, direction = -1,\n                                     min_slope = min_slope)\n  }\n  k <- length(pts)\n  if (!is.finite(b)) {\n    pts[k] <- .expand_to_valid_tail(pts[k], hprime, b, direction = 1,\n                                     min_slope = min_slope)\n  }\n\n  pts <- sort(unique(pts))\n  if (length(pts) < 2) {\n    stop(\"Failed to construct at least 2 distinct starting abscissae; \",\n         \"try supplying `x_init` explicitly.\", call. = FALSE)\n  }\n  pts\n}\n\n## -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n## 4. Building the piecewise-linear upper/lower hulls\n## -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#' Check that h' is non-increasing across sorted abscissae (necessary\n#' condition for h = log f to be concave). Raises an error otherwise.\n.check_log_concavity <- function(absc, hpx, tol) {\n  if (length(absc) < 2) return(invisible(TRUE))\n  d <- diff(hpx)\n  if (any(d > tol)) {\n    bad <- which(d > tol)[1]\n    stop(sprintf(paste0(\n      \"Non-log-concave density detected: the derivative of log(f) \",\n      \"increased between x = %.6g and x = %.6g (h'=%.6g then h'=%.6g). \",\n      \"Adaptive rejection sampling requires a log-concave density.\"),\n      absc[bad], absc[bad + 1], hpx[bad], hpx[bad + 1]), call. = FALSE)\n  }\n  invisible(TRUE)\n}\n\n#' Construct the upper-hull tangent-line intersection points z_1..z_{k-1}\n#' and the domain-bounded piece boundaries. Detects out-of-order\n#' intersections, another symptom of a non-log-concave density.\n.compute_intersections <- function(absc, hx, hpx, domain, tol) {\n  k <- length(absc)\n  if (k == 1) return(numeric(0))\n  z <- numeric(k - 1)\n  for (i in seq_len(k - 1)) {\n    den <- hpx[i] - hpx[i + 1]\n    if (abs(den) < 1e-12) {\n      z[i] <- (absc[i] + absc[i + 1]) / 2\n    } else {\n      num <- (hx[i + 1] - hx[i]) - (absc[i + 1] * hpx[i + 1] - absc[i] * hpx[i])\n      z[i] <- num / den\n    }\n    if (z[i] < absc[i] - tol || z[i] > absc[i + 1] + tol) {\n      stop(sprintf(\n        \"Non-log-concave density detected: tangent lines at x = %.6g and \",\n        \"x = %.6g intersect out of order (z = %.6g). Adaptive rejection \",\n        \"sampling requires a log-concave density.\",\n        absc[i], absc[i + 1], z[i]), call. = FALSE)\n    }\n    z[i] <- min(max(z[i], absc[i]), absc[i + 1])\n  }\n  z\n}\n\n#' Build the full hull representation used for sampling: per-piece slope,\n#' intercept, and probability mass (integral of exp(upper hull)).\n.build_hull <- function(absc, hx, hpx, domain, concavity_tol = 1e-3) {\n  .check_log_concavity(absc, hpx, concavity_tol)\n  z <- .compute_intersections(absc, hx, hpx, domain, tol = 1e-6)\n  k <- length(absc)\n  bounds <- c(domain[1], z, domain[2])\n  baseline <- max(hx)\n  const <- hx - baseline # tangent-line intercepts relative to baseline\n\n  min_slope <- 1e-10\n  masses <- numeric(k)\n  for (i in seq_len(k)) {\n    lo <- bounds[i]; hi <- bounds[i + 1]\n    m <- hpx[i]\n    explo <- if (is.infinite(lo)) 0 else exp(const[i] + m * (lo - absc[i]))\n    exphi <- if (is.infinite(hi)) 0 else exp(const[i] + m * (hi - absc[i]))\n    masses[i] <- if (abs(m) < min_slope) {\n      (hi - lo) * exp(const[i])\n    } else {\n      (exphi - explo) / m\n    }\n  }\n\n  list(absc = absc, hx = hx, hpx = hpx, z = z, bounds = bounds,\n       baseline = baseline, const = const, masses = masses, domain = domain)\n}\n\n## -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n## 5. Evaluating the hulls\n## -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#' Evaluate the piecewise-linear upper hull u(x) at a single point x,\n#' given which piece index x falls in.\n.upper_hull_piece <- function(hull, i) {\n  hull$hx[i] + 0 # placeholder for readability; real eval is in .eval_upper\n}\n\n.eval_upper_hull <- function(hull, x) {\n  i <- findInterval(x, hull$bounds, rightmost.closed = TRUE)\n  i <- min(max(i, 1L), length(hull$absc))\n  hull$hx[i] + hull$hpx[i] * (x - hull$absc[i])\n}\n\n#' Evaluate the piecewise-linear lower hull (squeeze) l(x). Returns -Inf\n#' outside the span of the current abscissae, as required by the method.\n.eval_lower_hull <- function(hull, x) {\n  absc <- hull$absc; hx <- hull$hx\n  k <- length(absc)\n  if (x <= absc[1] || x >= absc[k]) return(-Inf)\n  i <- findInterval(x, absc, rightmost.closed = TRUE)\n  i <- min(max(i, 1L), k - 1L)\n  lo <- absc[i]; hi <- absc[i + 1]\n  ((hi - x) * hx[i] + (x - lo) * hx[i + 1]) / (hi - lo)\n}\n\n## -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n## 6. Sampling from the upper hull\n## -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#' Draw one point from the piecewise-exponential upper hull via inverse-CDF\n#' sampling. Returns the draw and the exact upper-hull log-value there\n#' (so callers never need to re-evaluate the upper hull separately).\n.sample_upper_hull <- function(hull) {\n  k <- length(hull$absc)\n  total <- sum(hull$masses)\n  probs <- hull$masses / total\n  piece <- sample.int(k, size = 1, prob = probs)\n\n  lo <- hull$bounds[piece]; hi <- hull$bounds[piece + 1]\n  m <- hull$hpx[piece]; x_i <- hull$absc[piece]; c_i <- hull$const[piece]\n  r <- runif(1)\n\n  min_slope <- 1e-10\n  if (abs(m) < min_slope) {\n    x_star <- lo + r * (hi - lo)\n  } else {\n    explo <- if (is.infinite(lo)) 0 else exp(c_i + m * (lo - x_i))\n    target <- explo + r * m * hull$masses[piece]\n    x_star <- x_i + (log(target) - c_i) / m\n  }\n  u_val <- hull$hx[piece] + hull$hpx[piece] * (x_star - x_i)\n  list(x = x_star, u = u_val)\n}\n\n## -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n## 7. Main driver\n## -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#' Adaptive rejection sampling (Gilks & Wild, 1992).\n#'\n#' @param n Number of samples to draw (positive integer).\n#' @param f A vectorized function computing the (possibly unnormalized)\n#'   density of interest, e.g. \\code{dnorm} or \\code{function(x) exp(-x^2)}.\n#'   \\code{f} must be log-concave on \\code{domain}.\n#' @param domain Length-2 numeric vector \\code{c(lower, upper)} giving the\n#'   support of the density. Defaults to the whole real line.\n#' @param x_init Optional numeric vector (length >= 2) of starting\n#'   abscissae strictly inside \\code{domain}. If omitted, ars() picks its\n#'   own starting points automatically.\n#' @param max_abscissae Safety cap on the number of hull points; exceeding\n#'   it signals a misbehaving density (default 500).\n#' @param max_iter Safety cap on the number of proposal draws (default\n#'   \\code{200 * n + 2000}).\n#' @param concavity_tol Numerical tolerance used when checking that the\n#'   derivative of log(f) is non-increasing (default 1e-3).\n#' @param verbose If TRUE, prints progress information.\n#'\n#' @return A numeric vector of \\code{n} samples, with an attached\n#'   \\code{\"diagnostics\"} attribute listing the number of proposals drawn\n#'   and the final number of abscissae used.\nars <- function(n, f, domain = c(-Inf, Inf), x_init = NULL,\n                 max_abscissae = 500, max_iter = NULL,\n                 concavity_tol = 1e-3, verbose = FALSE) {\n  .validate_ars_inputs(n, f, domain, x_init)\n  n <- as.integer(round(n))\n  if (is.null(max_iter)) max_iter <- 200L * n + 2000L\n\n  logf <- .make_log_density(f, domain)\n  hprime <- .make_log_density_derivative(logf, domain)\n\n  absc <- .initialize_abscissae(hprime, domain, x_init)\n  hx <- logf(absc)\n  hpx <- hprime(absc)\n  if (any(!is.finite(hx))) {\n    stop(\"log(f(x)) is not finite at the starting abscissae; supply \",\n         \"`x_init` points where the density is strictly positive.\",\n         call. = FALSE)\n  }\n  hull <- .build_hull(absc, hx, hpx, domain, concavity_tol)\n\n  samples <- numeric(n)\n  n_accepted <- 0L\n  n_proposals <- 0L\n\n  while (n_accepted < n) {\n    if (n_proposals >= max_iter) {\n      stop(sprintf(\n        \"Exceeded max_iter = %d proposals after accepting %d/%d samples. \",\n        \"This may indicate the density is not log-concave, or that \",\n        \"`domain` is misspecified.\", max_iter, n_accepted, n), call. = FALSE)\n    }\n    n_proposals <- n_proposals + 1L\n\n    draw <- .sample_upper_hull(hull)\n    x_star <- draw$x\n    u_star <- draw$u\n    w <- runif(1)\n    l_star <- .eval_lower_hull(hull, x_star)\n\n    if (log(w) <= l_star - u_star) {\n      n_accepted <- n_accepted + 1L\n      samples[n_accepted] <- x_star\n      next\n    }\n\n    hx_star <- logf(x_star)\n    hpx_star <- hprime(x_star)\n\n    if (log(w) <= hx_star - u_star) {\n      n_accepted <- n_accepted + 1L\n      samples[n_accepted] <- x_star\n    }\n\n    absc <- c(hull$absc, x_star)\n    ord <- order(absc)\n    absc <- absc[ord]\n    hx <- c(hull$hx, hx_star)[ord]\n    hpx <- c(hull$hpx, hpx_star)[ord]\n    if (length(absc) > max_abscissae) {\n      stop(sprintf(\n        \"Number of hull abscissae exceeded max_abscissae = %d. This \",\n        \"usually indicates the density is not log-concave.\",\n        max_abscissae), call. = FALSE)\n    }\n    hull <- .build_hull(absc, hx, hpx, domain, concavity_tol)\n\n    if (verbose && n_accepted %% max(1L, n %/% 10L) == 0L) {\n      message(sprintf(\"ars: %d/%d accepted, %d proposals, %d abscissae\",\n                       n_accepted, n, n_proposals, length(absc)))\n    }\n  }\n\n  attr(samples, \"diagnostics\") <- list(\n    n_proposals = n_proposals,\n    n_abscissae_final = length(hull$absc),\n    acceptance_rate = n / n_proposals\n  )\n  samples\n}\n\n## -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n## 8. Test suite\n## -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#' Print one PASS/FAIL line for a distributional test and return whether it\n#' passed.\n.report_distribution_test <- function(name, samples, mean_theo, sd_theo,\n                                       cdf_theo, mean_tol_sd = 5,\n                                       sd_rel_tol = 0.2, ks_alpha = 0.01) {\n  n <- length(samples)\n  mean_hat <- mean(samples)\n  sd_hat <- sd(samples)\n\n  se_mean <- sd_theo / sqrt(n)\n  mean_ok <- abs(mean_hat - mean_theo) <= mean_tol_sd * se_mean\n  sd_ok <- abs(sd_hat - sd_theo) / sd_theo <= sd_rel_tol\n  ks <- suppressWarnings(ks.test(samples, cdf_theo))\n  ks_ok <- ks$p.value >= ks_alpha\n\n  pass <- mean_ok && sd_ok && ks_ok\n  cat(sprintf(\n    \"%s: %s | n=%d mean=%.4f (theoretical=%.4f) sd=%.4f (theoretical=%.4f) KS_p=%.4f\\n\",\n    name, if (pass) \"PASS\" else \"FAIL\", n, mean_hat, mean_theo, sd_hat,\n    sd_theo, add(.report_error_test(\"TEST_INVALID_DOMAIN_ORDER\",\n        ars(10, dnorm, domain = c(5, -5))))\n  add(.report_error_test(\"TEST_DOMAIN_MISMATCHES_SUPPORT\",\n        ars(10, dexp, domain = c(-100, -10))))\n  cat(\"\\n\")\n\n  cat(\"--- Log-concavity detection tests (expect an error) ---\\n\")\n  bimodal <- function(x) 0.5 * dnorm(x, -4, 1) + 0.5 * dnorm(x, 4, 1)\n  add(.report_error_test(\"TEST_REJECTS_BIMODAL_MIXTURE\",\n        ars(200, bimodal, domain = c(-Inf, Inf))))\n  add(.report_error_test(\"TEST_REJECTS_HEAVY_TAILED_T3\",\n        ars(200, function(x) dt(x, df = 3), domain = c(-Inf, Inf))))\n  cat(\"\\n\")\n\n  cat(\"--- Sampling from known log-concave distributions ---\\n\")\n  n <- 3000\n\n  s_norm <- ars(n, dnorm, domain = c(-Inf, Inf))\n  add(.report_distribution_test(\"TEST_STANDARD_NORMAL\", s_norm,\n        mean_theo = 0, sd_theo = 1, cdf_theo = \"pnorm\"))\n\n  s_norm2 <- ars(n, function(x) dnorm(x, mean = 5, sd = 2),\n                 domain = c(-Inf, Inf))\n  add(.report_distribution_test(\"TEST_NORMAL_MEAN5_SD2\", s_norm2,\n        mean_theo = 5, sd_theo = 2,\n        cdf_theo = function(x) pnorm(x, mean = 5, sd = 2)))\n\n  s_exp <- ars(n, function(x) dexp(x, rate = 2), domain = c(0, Inf))\n  add(.report_distribution_test(\"TEST_EXPONENTIAL_RATE2\", s_exp,\n        mean_theo = 1 / 2, sd_theo = 1 / 2,\n        cdf_theo = function(x) pexp(x, rate = 2)))\n\n  s_gamma <- ars(n, function(x) dgamma(x, shape = 3, rate = 1),\n                 domain = c(0, Inf))\n  add(.report_distribution_test(\"TEST_GAMMA_SHAPE3_RATE1\", s_gamma,\n        mean_theo = 3, sd_theo = sqrt(3),\n        cdf_theo = function(x) pgamma(x, shape = 3, rate = 1)))\n  cat(\"\\n\")\n\n  cat(\"--- Module-level tests ---\\n\")\n  add(.report_module_tests())\n  cat(\"\\n\")\n\n  writeLines(format(s_norm, digits = 10), \"/app/normal_samples.txt\")\n  writeLines(format(s_exp, digits = 10), \"/app/exponential_samples.txt\")\n  cat(\"Wrote /app/normal_samples.txt and /app/exponential_samples.txt\\n\\n\")\n\n  n_pass <- sum(results)\n  n_total <- length(results)\n  cat(\"=======================================================\\n\")\n  cat(sprintf(\"SUMMARY: %d/%d tests passed\\n\", n_pass, n_total))\n  cat(\"=======================================================\\n\")\n  invisible(n_pass == n_total)\n}\n\n#' Focused unit tests for the individual hull-building helper functions,\n#' checked against hand-computed values for a simple known case.\n.report_module_tests <- function() {\n  pass_all <- TRUE\n\n  # Two tangent points on h(x) = -x^2/2 (standard normal, unnormalized):\n  # h(x) = -x^2/2, At x = -1: h=-0.5, h'=1. At x = 1: h=-0.5, h'=-1.\n  absc <- c(-1, 1); hx <- c(-0.5, -0.5); hpx <- c(1, -1)\n  z <- .compute_intersections(absc, hx, hpx, c(-Inf, Inf), tol = 1e-6)\n  ok1 <- isTRUE(all.equal(z, 0, tolerance = 1e-8))\n  cat(sprintf(\"  intersection_point_symmetric_case: %s (z=%.6f, expected 0)\\n\",\n              if (ok1) \"PASS\" else \"FAIL\", z))\n  pass_all <- pass_all && ok1\n\n  hull <- .build_hull(absc, hx, hpx, c(-Inf, Inf))\n  u_at_0 <- .eval_upper_hull(hull, 0)\n  ok2 <- isTRUE(all.equal(u_at_0, -0.5, tolerance = 1e-8))\n  cat(sprintf(\"  upper_hull_value_at_tangent_boundary: %s (u(0)=%.6f, expected -0.5)\\n\",\n              if (ok2) \"PASS\" else \"FAIL\", u_at_0))\n  pass_all <- pass_all && ok2\n\n  l_at_0 <- .eval_lower_hull(hull, 0)\n  ok3 <- isTRUE(all.equal(l_at_0, -0.5, tolerance = 1e-8))\n  cat(sprintf(\"  lower_hull_value_at_midpoint: %s (l(0)=%.6f, expected -0.5)\\n\",\n              if (ok3) \"PASS\" else \"FAIL\", l_at_0))\n  pass_all <- pass_all && ok3\n\n  l_outside <- .eval_lower_hull(hull, 5)\n  ok4 <- is.infinite(l_outside) && l_outside < 0\n  cat(sprintf(\"  lower_hull_is_negative_infinity_outside_span: %s\\n\",\n              if (ok4) \"PASS\" else \"FAIL\"))\n  pass_all <- pass_all && ok4\n\n  logf <- .make_log_density(dnorm, c(-Inf, Inf))\n  hprime <- .make_log_density_derivative(logf, c(-Inf, Inf))\n  deriv_at_0 <- hprime(0)\n  ok5 <- isTRUE(all.equal(deriv_at_0, 0, tolerance = 1e-3))\n  cat(sprintf(\"  numerical_derivative_matches_analytic_at_mode: %s (h'(0)=%.6f, expected 0)\\n\",\n              if (ok5) \"PASS\" else \"FAIL\", deriv_at_0))\n  pass_all <- pass_all && ok5\n\n  deriv_at_1 <- hprime(1)\n  ok6 <- isTRUE(all.equal(deriv_at_1, -1, tolerance = 1e-3))\n  cat(sprintf(\"  numerical_derivative_matches_analytic_at_one: %s (h'(1)=%.6f, expected -1)\\n\",\n              if (ok6) \"PASS\" else \"FAIL\", deriv_at_1))\n  pass_all <- pass_all && ok6\n\n  pass_all\n}\n\nif (sys.nframe() == 0 && !interactive()) {\n  # All helpers are pure functions of their arguments\n# (no shared mutable state), which keeps them independently testable.\n# ==============================================================================\n\n## -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n## 1. Input validation\n## -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#' Validate the arguments to ars() before any sampling work begins.\n.validate_ars_inputs <- function(n, f, domain, x_init) {\n  if (!is.function(f)) {\n    stop(\"`f` must be a function that evaluates the (possibly unnormalized) \",\n         \"density, e.g. dnorm.\", call. = FALSE)\n  }\n  if (!is.numeric(n) || length(n) != 1 || is.na(n) || n <= 0 ||\n      n != round(n)) {\n    stop(\"`n` must be a single positive integer (number of samples).\",\n         call. = FALSE)\n  }\n  if (!is.numeric(domain) || length(domain) != 2 || any(is.na(domain))) {\n    stop(\"`domain` must be a numeric vector of length 2: c(lower, upper).\",\n         call. = FALSE)\n  }\n  if (domain[1] >= domain[2]) {\n    stop(\"`domain` lower bound must be strictly less than the upper bound.\",\n         call. = FALSE)\n  }\n  if (!is.null(x_init)) {\n    if (!is.numeric(x_init) || length(x_init) < 2 || any(is.na(x_init))) {\n      stop(\"`x_init` must be a numeric vector with at least 2 finite values.\",\n           call. = FALSE)\n    }\n    if (any(x_init <= domain[1]) || any(x_init >= domain[2])) {\n      stop(\"All `x_init` points must lie strictly inside `domain`.\",\n           call. = FALSE)\n    }\n  }\n\n  # Sanity-check that f behaves like a density: non-negative, finite, and\n  # not identically zero on a handful of probe points inside the domain.\n  probe <- .probe_points(domain, x_init)\n  vals <- suppressWarnings(f(probe))\n  if (!is.numeric(vals) || length(vals) != length(probe)) {\n    stop(\"`f` must be vectorized: given a numeric vector it must return a \",\n         \"numeric vector of the same length.\", call. = FALSE)\n  }\n  if (any(is.na(vals)) || any(vals < 0)) {\n    stop(\"`f` returned NA or negative values; it must be a valid \",\n         \"(possibly unnormalized) density.\", call. = FALSE)\n  }\n  if (all(vals == 0)) {\n    stop(\"`f` evaluates to 0 everywhere it was probed inside `domain`; \",\n         \"check that `domain` matches the support of the density.\",\n         call. = FALSE)\n  }\n  invisible(TRUE)\n}\n\n#' A handful of points inside `domain` used to sanity-check `f`.\n.probe_points <- function(domain, x_init) {\n  a <- domain[1]; b <- domain[2]\n  if (!is.null(x_init)) return(x_init)\n  if (is.finite(a) && is.finite(b)) {\n    a + (b - a) * c(0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9)\n  } else if (is.finite(a)) {\n    a + c(0.5, 1, 2, 5)\n  } else if (is.finite(b)) {\n    b - c(0.5, 1, 2, 5)\n  } else {\n    c(-5, -1, 0, 1, 5)\n  }\n}\n\n## -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n## 2. Log-density and numerical derivative\n## -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#' Build a (possibly unnormalized) log-density function from f, clamped to\n#' `domain` so that log(0) outside the support does not propagate as NaN.\n.make_log_density <- function(f, domain) {\n  function(x) {\n    val <- rep(-Inf, length(x))\n    inside <- x > domain[1] & x < domain[2]\n    if (any(inside)) {\n      fx <- f(x[inside])\n      val[inside] <- log(fx)\n    }\n    val\n  }\n}\n\n#' Central-difference numerical derivative of `logf`, clamped to stay\n#' strictly inside `domain` so evaluation never lands outside the support.\n.make_log_density_derivative <- function(logf, domain) {\n  function(x) {\n    eps <- pmax(1e-6, abs(x) * 1e-5)\n    lo <- pmax(x - eps, domain[1] + 1e-10)\n    hi <- pmin(x + eps, domain[2] - 1e-10)\n    h <- pmax(hi - lo, 1e-12)\n    (logf(hi) - logf(lo)) / h\n  }\n}\n\n## -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n## 3. Choosing starting abscissae\n## -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#' Expand `x` outward (in the given direction) until `hprime` has the sign\n#' required for the tail to be integrable, or until the finite domain bound\n#' is reached (in which case no sign condition is required).\n.expand_to_valid_tail <- function(x, hprime, bound, direction, min_slope,\n                                   max_iter = 60) {\n  step <- max(1, abs(x))\n  for (i in seq_len(max_iter)) {\n    slope <- hprime(x)\n    ok <- if (direction > 0) slope <= -min_slope else slope >= min_slope\n    if (ok) return(x)\n    x_next <- x + direction * step\n    if (direction > 0 && x_next >= bound) {\n      if (is.finite(bound)) return(bound - 1e-6 * max(1, abs(bound)))\n    }\n    if (direction < 0 && x_next <= bound) {\n      if (is.finite(bound)) return(bound + 1e-6 * max(1, abs(bound)))\n    }\n    x <- x_next\n    step <- step * 2\n  }\n  stop(\"Could not find a starting point with the required tail behavior \",\n       \"(h'(x) must eventually change sign away from the mode). This \",\n       \"usually means the density is not log-concave, or its tails decay \",\n       \"too slowly.\", call. = FALSE)\n}\n\n#' Choose initial abscissae satisfying the ARS boundary requirements:\n#' h'(x1) > 0 if the domain is unbounded below, h'(xk) < 0 if unbounded\n#' above. Interior guesses are used as-is (and refined by later hull\n#' updates during sampling).\n.initialize_abscissae <- function(hprime, domain, x_init, min_slope = 1e-8) {\n  a <- domain[1]; b <- domain[2]\n\n  if (!is.null(x_init)) {\n    pts <- sort(unique(x_init))\n  } else if (is.finite(a) && is.finite(b)) {\n    pts <- a + (b - a) * c(0.25, 0.75)\n  } else if (is.finite(a)) {\n    pts <- a + c(0.5, 2)\n  } else if (is.finite(b)) {\n    pts <- b - c(2, 0.5)\n  } else {\n    pts <- c(-1, 1)\n  }\n\n  if (!is.finite(a)) {\n    pts[1] <- .expand_to_valid_tail(pts[1], hprime, a, direction = -1,\n                                     min_slope = min_slope)\n  }\n  k <- length(pts)\n  if (!is.finite(b)) {\n    pts[k] <- .expand_to_valid_tail(pts[k], hprime, b, direction = 1,\n                                     min_slope = min_slope)\n  }\n\n  pts <- sort(unique(pts))\n  if (length(pts) < 2) {\n    stop(\"Failed to construct at least 2 distinct starting abscissae; \",\n         \"try supplying `x_init` explicitly.\", call. = FALSE)\n  }\n  pts\n}\n\n## -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n## 4. Building the piecewise-linear upper/lower hulls\n## -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#' Check that h' is non-increasing across sorted abscissae (necessary\n#' condition for h = log f to be concave). Raises an error otherwise.\n.check_log_concavity <- function(absc, hpx, tol) {\n  if (length(absc) < 2) return(invisible(TRUE))\n  d <- diff(hpx)\n  if (any(d > tol)) {\n    bad <- which(d > tol)[1]\n    stop(sprintf(paste0(\n      \"Non-log-concave density detected: the derivative of log(f) \",\n      \"increased between x = %.6g and x = %.6g (h'=%.6g then h'=%.6g). \",\n      \"Adaptive rejection sampling requires a log-concave density.\"),\n      absc[bad], absc[bad + 1], hpx[bad], hpx[bad + 1]), call. = FALSE)\n  }\n  invisible(TRUE)\n}\n\n#' Construct the upper-hull tangent-line intersection points z_1..z_{k-1}\n#' and the domain-bounded piece boundaries. Detects out-of-order\n#' intersections, another symptom of a non-log-concave density.\n.compute_intersections <- function(absc, hx, hpx, domain, tol) {\n  k <- length(absc)\n  if (k == 1) return(numeric(0))\n  z <- numeric(k - 1)\n  for (i in seq_len(k - 1)) {\n    den <- hpx[i] - hpx[i + 1]\n    if (abs(den) < 1e-12) {\n      z[i] <- (absc[i] + absc[i + 1]) / 2\n    } else {\n      num <- (hx[i + 1] - hx[i]) - (absc[i + 1] * hpx[i + 1] - absc[i] * hpx[i])\n      z[i] <- num / den\n    }\n    if (z[i] < absc[i] - tol || z[i] > absc[i + 1] + tol) {\n      stop(sprintf(paste0(\n        \"Non-log-concave density detected: tangent lines at x = %.6g and \",\n        \"x = %.6g intersect out of order (z = %.6g). Adaptive rejection \",\n        \"sampling requires a log-concave density.\"),\n        absc[i], absc[i + 1], z[i]), call. = FALSE)\n    }\n    z[i] <- min(max(z[i], absc[i]), absc[i + 1])\n  }\n  z\n}\n\n#' Build the full hull representation used for sampling: per-piece slope,\n#' intercept, and probability mass (integral of exp(upper hull)).\n.build_hull <- function(absc, hx, hpx, domain, concavity_tol = 1e-3) {\n  .check_log_concavity(absc, hpx, concavity_tol)\n  z <- .compute_intersections(absc, hx, hpx, domain, tol = 1e-6)\n  k <- length(absc)\n  bounds <- c(domain[1], z, domain[2])\n  baseline <- max(hx)\n  const <- hx - baseline # tangent-line intercepts relative to baseline\n\n  min_slope <- 1e-10\n  masses <- numeric(k)\n  for (i in seq_len(k)) {\n    lo <- bounds[i]; hi <- bounds[i + 1]\n    m <- hpx[i]\n    explo <- if (is.infinite(lo)) 0 else exp(const[i] + m * (lo - absc[i]))\n    exphi <- if (is.infinite(hi)) 0 else exp(const[i] + m * (hi - absc[i]))\n    masses[i] <- if (abs(m) < min_slope) {\n      (hi - lo) * exp(const[i])\n    } else {\n      (exphi - explo) / m\n    }\n  }\n\n  list(absc = absc, hx = hx, hpx = hpx, z = z, bounds = bounds,\n       baseline = baseline, const = const, masses = masses, domain = domain)\n}\n\n## -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n## 5. Evaluating the hulls\n## -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#' Evaluate the piecewise-linear upper hull u(x) at a single point x,\n#' given which piece index x falls in.\n.upper_hull_piece <- function(hull, i) {\n  hull$hx[i] + 0 # placeholder for readability; real eval is in .eval_upper\n}\n\n.eval_upper_hull <- function(hull, x) {\n  i <- findInterval(x, hull$bounds, rightmost.closed = TRUE)\n  i <- min(max(i, 1L), length(hull$absc))\n  hull$hx[i] + hull$hpx[i] * (x - hull$absc[i])\n}\n\n#' Evaluate the piecewise-linear lower hull (squeeze) l(x). Returns -Inf\n#' outside the span of the current abscissae, as required by the method.\n.eval_lower_hull <- function(hull, x) {\n  absc <- hull$absc; hx <- hull$hx\n  k <- length(absc)\n  if (x <= absc[1] || x >= absc[k]) return(-Inf)\n  i <- findInterval(x, absc, rightmost.closed = TRUE)\n  i <- min(max(i, 1L), k - 1L)\n  lo <- absc[i]; hi <- absc[i + 1]\n  ((hi - x) * hx[i] + (x - lo) * hx[i + 1]) / (hi - lo)\n}\n\n## -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n## 6. Sampling from the upper hull\n## -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#' Draw one point from the piecewise-exponential upper hull via inverse-CDF\n#' sampling. Returns the draw and the exact upper-hull log-value there\n#' (so callers never need to re-evaluate the upper hull separately).\n.sample_upper_hull <- function(hull) {\n  k <- length(hull$absc)\n  total <- sum(hull$masses)\n  probs <- hull$masses / total\n  piece <- sample.int(k, size = 1, prob = probs)\n\n  lo <- hull$bounds[piece]; hi <- hull$bounds[piece + 1]\n  m <- hull$hpx[piece]; x_i <- hull$absc[piece]; c_i <- hull$const[piece]\n  r <- runif(1)\n\n  min_slope <- 1e-10\n  if (abs(m) < min_slope) {\n    x_star <- lo + r * (hi - lo)\n  } else {\n    explo <- if (is.infinite(lo)) 0 else exp(c_i + m * (lo - x_i))\n    target <- explo + r * m * hull$masses[piece]\n    x_star <- x_i + (log(target) - c_i) / m\n  }\n  u_val <- hull$hx[piece] + hull$hpx[piece] * (x_star - x_i)\n  list(x = x_star, u = u_val)\n}\n\n## -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n## 7. Main driver\n## -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#' Adaptive rejection sampling (Gilks & Wild, 1992).\n#'\n#' @param n Number of samples to draw (positive integer).\n#' @param f A vectorized function computing the (possibly unnormalized)\n#'   density of interest, e.g. \\code{dnorm} or \\code{function(x) exp(-x^2)}.\n#'   \\code{f} must be log-concave on \\code{domain}.\n#' @param domain Length-2 numeric vector \\code{c(lower, upper)} giving the\n#'   support of the density. Defaults to the whole real line.\n#' @param x_init Optional numeric vector (length >= 2) of starting\n#'   abscissae strictly inside \\code{domain}. If omitted, ars() picks its\n#'   own starting points automatically.\n#' @param max_abscissae Safety cap on the number of hull points; exceeding\n#'   it signals a misbehaving density (default 500).\n#' @param max_iter Safety cap on the number of proposal draws (default\n#'   \\code{200 * n + 2000}).\n#' @param concavity_tol Numerical tolerance used when checking that the\n#'   derivative of log(f) is non-increasing (default 1e-3).\n#' @param verbose If TRUE, prints progress information.\n#'\n#' @return A numeric vector of \\code{n} samples, with an attached\n#'   \\code{\"diagnostics\"} attribute listing the number of proposals drawn\n#'   and the final number of abscissae used.\nars <- function(n, f, domain = c(-Inf, Inf), x_init = NULL,\n                 max_abscissae = 500, max_iter = NULL,\n                 concavity_tol = 1e-3, verbose = FALSE) {\n  .validate_ars_inputs(n, f, domain, x_init)\n  n <- as.integer(round(n))\n  if (is.null(max_iter)) max_iter <- 200L * n + 2000L\n\n  logf <- .make_log_density(f, domain)\n  hprime <- .make_log_density_derivative(logf, domain)\n\n  absc <- .initialize_abscissae(hprime, domain, x_init)\n  hx <- logf(absc)\n  hpx <- hprime(absc)\n  if (any(!is.finite(hx))) {\n    stop(\"log(f(x)) is not finite at the starting abscissae; supply \",\n         \"`x_init` points where the density is strictly positive.\",\n         call. = FALSE)\n  }\n  hull <- .build_hull(absc, hx, hpx, domain, concavity_tol)\n\n  samples <- numeric(n)\n  n_accepted <- 0L\n  n_proposals <- 0L\n\n  while (n_accepted < n) {\n    if (n_proposals >= max_iter) {\n      stop(sprintf(\n        \"Exceeded max_iter = %d proposals after accepting %d/%d samples. \",\n        \"This may indicate the density is not log-concave, or that \",\n        \"`domain` is misspecified.\", max_iter, n_accepted, n), call. = FALSE)\n    }\n    n_proposals <- n_proposals + 1L\n\n    draw <- .sample_upper_hull(hull)\n    x_star <- draw$x\n    u_star <- draw$u\n    w <- runif(1)\n    l_star <- .eval_lower_hull(hull, x_star)\n\n    if (log(w) <= l_star - u_star) {\n      n_accepted <- n_accepted + 1L\n      samples[n_accepted] <- x_star\n      next\n    }\n\n    hx_star <- logf(x_star)\n    hpx_star <- hprime(x_star)\n\n    if (log(w) <= hx_star - u_star) {\n      n_accepted <- n_accepted + 1L\n      samples[n_accepted] <- x_star\n    }\n\n    absc <- c(hull$absc, x_star)\n    ord <- order(absc)\n    absc <- absc[ord]\n    hx <- c(hull$hx, hx_star)[ord]\n    hpx <- c(hull$hpx, hpx_star)[ord]\n    if (length(absc) > max_abscissae) {\n      stop(sprintf(\n        \"Number of hull abscissae exceeded max_abscissae = %d. This \",\n        \"usually indicates the density is not log-concave.\",\n        max_abscissae), call. = FALSE)\n    }\n    hull <- .build_hull(absc, hx, hpx, domain, concavity_tol)\n\n    if (verbose && n_accepted %% max(1L, n %/% 10L) == 0L) {\n      message(sprintf(\"ars: %d/%d accepted, %d proposals, %d abscissae\",\n                       n_accepted, n, n_proposals, length(absc)))\n    }\n  }\n\n  attr(samples, \"diagnostics\") <- list(\n    n_proposals = n_proposals,\n    n_abscissae_final = length(hull$absc),\n    acceptance_rate = n / n_proposals\n  )\n  samples\n}\n\n## -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n## 8. Test suite\n## -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#' Print one PASS/FAIL line for a distributional test and return whether it\n#' passed.\n.report_distribution_test <- function(name, samples, mean_theo, sd_theo,\n                                       cdf_theo, mean_tol_sd = 5,\n                                       sd_rel_tol = 0.2, ks_alpha = 0.01) {\n  n <- length(samples)\n  mean_hat <- mean(samples)\n  sd_hat <- sd(samples)\n\n  se_mean <- sd_theo / sqrt(n)\n  mean_ok <- abs(mean_hat - mean_theo) <= mean_tol_sd * se_mean\n  sd_ok <- abs(sd_hat - sd_theo) / sd_theo <= sd_rel_tol\n  ks <- suppressWarnings(ks.test(samples, cdf_theo))\n  ks_ok <- ks$p.value >= ks_alpha\n\n  pass <- mean_ok && sd_ok && ks_ok\n  cat(sprintf(\n    \"%s: %s | n=%d mean=%.4f (theoretical=%.4f) sd=%.4f (theoretical=%.4f) KS_p=%.4f\\n\",\n    name, if (pass) \"PASS\" else \"FAIL\", n, mean_hat, mean_theo, sd_hat,\n    sd_theo, ks$p.value))\n  pass\n}\n\n#' Print one PASS/FAIL line for a test that expects ars() to raise an error\n#' (e.g. invalid inputs, or a non-log-concave density).\n.report_error_test <- function(name, expr) {\n  result <- tryCatch({ force(expr); \"no_error\" },\n                      error = function(e) conditionMessage(e))\n  pass <- !identical(result, \"no_error\")\n  msg <- if (pass) result else \"expected an error but none was raised\"\n  cat(sprintf(\"%s: %s | %s\\n\", name, if (pass) \"PASS\" else \"FAIL\", msg))\n  pass\n}\n\n#' Run the full ars() test suite and print PASS/FAIL results for each test.\n#' Also writes sample draws from the normal and exponential tests to\n#' normal_samples.txt and exponential_samples.txt for inspection.\ntest <- function() {\n  set.seed(20240613)\n  results <- logical(0)\n  add <- function(x) results <<- c(results, x)\n\n  cat(\"=======================================================\\n\")\n  cat(\"Adaptive Rejection Sampling (Gilks & Wild, 1992) -- tests\\n\")\n  cat(\"=======================================================\\n\\n\")\n\n  cat(\"--- Input validation tests ---\\n\")\n  add(.report_error_test(\"TEST_NEGATIVE_N\",\n        ars(-5, dnorm)))\n  add(.report_error_test(\"TEST_ZERO_N\",\n        ars(0, dnorm)))\n  add(.report_error_test(\"TEST_NON_FUNCTION_F\",\n        ars(10, \"not_a_function\")))\n  add(.report_error_test(\"TEST_INVALID_DOMAIN_ORDER\",\n        ars(10, dnorm, domain = c(5, -5))))\n  add(.report_error_test(\"TEST_DOMAIN_MISMATCHES_SUPPORT\",\n        ars(10, dexp, domain = c(-100, -10))))\n  cat(\"\\n\")\n\n  cat(\"--- Log-concavity detection tests (expect an error) ---\\n\")\n  bimodal <- function(x) 0.5 * dnorm(x, -4, 1) + 0.5 * dnorm(x, 4, 1)\n  add(.report_error_test(\"TEST_REJECTS_BIMODAL_MIXTURE\",\n        ars(200, bimodal, domain = c(-Inf, Inf))))\n  add(.report_error_test(\"TEST_REJECTS_HEAVY_TAILED_T3\",\n        ars(200, function(x) dt(x, df = 3), domain = c(-Inf, Inf))))\n  cat(\"\\n\")\n\n  cat(\"--- Sampling from known log-concave distributions ---\\n\")\n  n <- 3000\n\n  s_norm <- ars(n, dnorm, domain = c(-Inf, Inf))\n  add(.report_distribution_test(\"TEST_STANDARD_NORMAL\", s_norm,\n        mean_theo = 0, sd_theo = 1, cdf_theo = \"pnorm\"))\n\n  s_norm2 <- ars(n, function(x) dnorm(x, mean = 5, sd = 2),\n                 domain = c(-Inf, Inf))\n  add(.report_distribution_test(\"TEST_NORMAL_MEAN5_SD2\", s_norm2,\n        mean_theo = 5, sd_theo = 2,\n        cdf_theo = function(x) pnorm(x, mean = 5, sd = 2)))\n\n  s_exp <- ars(n, function(x) dexp(x, rate = 2), domain = c(0, Inf))\n  add(.report_distribution_test(\"TEST_EXPONENTIAL_RATE2\", s_exp,\n        mean_theo = 1 / 2, sd_theo = 1 / 2,\n        cdf_theo = function(x) pexp(x, rate = 2)))\n\n  s_gamma <- ars(n, function(x) dgamma(x, shape = 3, rate = 1),\n                 domain = c(0, Inf))\n  add(.report_distribution_test(\"TEST_GAMMA_SHAPE3_RATE1\", s_gamma,\n        mean_theo = 3, sd_theo = sqrt(3),\n        cdf_theo = function(x) pgamma(x, shape = 3, rate = 1)))\n  cat(\"\\n\")\n\n  cat(\"--- Module-level tests ---\\n\")\n  add(.report_module_tests())\n  cat(\"\\n\")\n\n  writeLines(format(s_norm, digits = 10), \"/app/normal_samples.txt\")\n  writeLines(format(s_exp, digits = 10), \"/app/exponential_samples.txt\")\n  cat(\"Wrote /app/normal_samples.txt and /app/exponential_samples.txt\\n\\n\")\n\n  n_pass <- sum(results)\n  n_total <- length(results)\n  cat(\"=======================================================\\n\")\n  cat(sprintf(\"SUMMARY: %d/%d tests passed\\n\", n_pass, n_total))\n  cat(\"=======================================================\\n\")\n  invisible(n_pass == n_total)\n}\n\n#' Focused unit tests for the individual hull-building helper functions,\n#' checked against hand-computed values for a simple known case.\n.report_module_tests <- function() {\n  pass_all <- TRUE\n\n  # Two tangent points on h(x) = -x^2/2 (standard normal, unnormalized):\n  # h(x) = -x^2/2, h'(x) = -x. At x = -1: h=-0.5, h'=1. At x = 1: h=-0.5, h'=-1.\n  absc <- c(-1, 1); hx <- c(-0.5, -0.5); hpx <- c(1, -1)\n  z <- .compute_intersections(absc, hx, hpx, c(-Inf, Inf), tol = 1e-6)\n  ok1 <- isTRUE(all.equal(z, 0, tolerance = 1e-8))\n  cat(sprintf(\"  intersection_point_symmetric_case: %s (z=%.6f, expected 0)\\n\",\n              if (ok1) \"PASS\" else \"FAIL\", z))\n  pass_all <- pass_all && ok1\n\n  hull <- .build_hull(absc, hx, hpx, c(-Inf, Inf))\n  u_at_0 <- .eval_upper_hull(hull, 0)\n  ok2 <- isTRUE(all.equal(u_at_0, -0.5, tolerance = 1e-8))\n  cat(sprintf(\"  upper_hull_value_at_tangent_boundary: %s (u(0)=%.6f, expected -0.5)\\n\",\n              if (ok2) \"PASS\" else \"FAIL\", u_at_0))\n  pass_all <- pass_all && ok2\n\n  l_at_0 <- .eval_lower_hull(hull, 0)\n  ok3 <- isTRUE(all.equal(l_at_0, -0.5, tolerance = 1e-8))\n  cat(sprintf(\"  lower_hull_value_at_midpoint: %s (l(0)=%.6f, expected -0.5)\\n\",\n              if (ok3) \"PASS\" else \"FAIL\", l_at_0))\n  pass_all <- pass_all && ok3\n\n  l_outside <- .eval_lower_hull(hull, 5)\n  ok4 <- is.infinite(l_outside) && l_outside < 0\n  cat(sprintf(\"  lower_hull_is_negative_infinity_outside_span: %s\\n\",\n              if (ok4) \"PASS\" else \"FAIL\"))\n  pass_all <- pass_all && ok4\n\n  logf <- .make_log_density(dnorm, c(-Inf, Inf))\n  hprime <- .make_log_density_derivative(logf, c(-Inf, Inf))\n  deriv_at_0 <- hprime(0)\n  ok5 <- isTRUE(all.equal(deriv_at_0, 0, tolerance = 1e-3))\n  cat(sprintf(\"  numerical_derivative_matches_analytic_at_mode: %s (h'(0)=%.6f, expected 0)\\n\",\n              if (ok5) \"PASS\" else \"FAIL\", deriv_at_0))\n  pass_all <- pass_all && ok5\n\n  deriv_at_1 <- hprime(1)\n  ok6 <- isTRUE(all.equal(deriv_at_1, -1, tolerance = 1e-3))\n  cat(sprintf(\"  numerical_derivative_matches_analytic_at_one: %s (h'(1)=%.6f, expected -1)\\n\",\n              if (ok6) \"PASS\" else \"FAIL\", deriv_at_1))\n  pass_all <- pass_all && ok6\n\n  pass_all\n}\n\nif (sys.nframe() == 0 && !interactive()) {\n  # This \",\n        \"usually indicates the density is not log-concave.\",\n        max_abscissae), call. = FALSE)","newString":"      stop(sprintf(paste0(\n        \"Number of hull abscissae exceeded max_abscissae = %d. This \",\n        \"usually indicates the density is not log-concave.\"),\n        max_abscissae), call. = FALSE)","originalFile":"# ==============================================================================\n# ars.R -- Adaptive Rejection Sampling (Gilks & Wild, 1992)\n#\n# Public API:\n#   ars(n, f, domain = c(-Inf, Inf), x_init = NULL, ...)  -- draw n samples\n#   test()                                                 -- run test suite\n#\n# The implementation is split into small, single-purpose helper functions\n# (prefixed with \".\") that mirror the structure of the Gilks & Wild algorithm:\n# building the piecewise-linear upper/lower hulls, sampling from the upper\n# hull, performing the squeeze/rejection tests, and updating the hull with\n# newly evaluated points. All helpers are pure functions of their arguments\n# (no shared mutable state), which keeps them independently testable.\n# ==============================================================================\n\n## -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n## 1. Input validation\n## -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#' Validate the arguments to ars() before any sampling work begins.\n.validate_ars_inputs <- function(n, f, domain, x_init) {\n  if (!is.function(f)) {\n    stop(\"`f` must be a function that evaluates the (possibly unnormalized) \",\n         \"density, e.g. dnorm.\", call. = FALSE)\n  }\n  if (!is.numeric(n) || length(n) != 1 || is.na(n) || n <= 0 ||\n      n != round(n)) {\n    stop(\"`n` must be a single positive integer (number of samples).\",\n         call. = FALSE)\n  }\n  if (!is.numeric(domain) || length(domain) != 2 || any(is.na(domain))) {\n    stop(\"`domain` must be a numeric vector of length 2: c(lower, upper).\",\n         call. = FALSE)\n  }\n  if (domain[1] >= domain[2]) {\n    stop(\"`domain` lower bound must be strictly less than the upper bound.\",\n         call. = FALSE)\n  }\n  if (!is.null(x_init)) {\n    if (!is.numeric(x_init) || length(x_init) < 2 || any(is.na(x_init))) {\n      stop(\"`x_init` must be a numeric vector with at least 2 finite values.\",\n           call. = FALSE)\n    }\n    if (any(x_init <= domain[1]) || any(x_init >= domain[2])) {\n      stop(\"All `x_init` points must lie strictly inside `domain`.\",\n           call. = FALSE)\n    }\n  }\n\n  # Sanity-check that f behaves like a density: non-negative, finite, and\n  # not identically zero on a handful of probe points inside the domain.\n  probe <- .probe_points(domain, x_init)\n  vals <- suppressWarnings(f(probe))\n  if (!is.numeric(vals) || length(vals) != length(probe)) {\n    stop(\"`f` must be vectorized: given a numeric vector it must return a \",\n         \"numeric vector of the same length.\", call. = FALSE)\n  }\n  if (any(is.na(vals)) || any(vals < 0)) {\n    stop(\"`f` returned NA or negative values; it must be a valid \",\n         \"(possibly unnormalized) density.\", call. = FALSE)\n  }\n  if (all(vals == 0)) {\n    stop(\"`f` evaluates to 0 everywhere it was probed inside `domain`; \",\n         \"check that `domain` matches the support of the density.\",\n         call. = FALSE)\n  }\n  invisible(TRUE)\n}\n\n#' A handful of points inside `domain` used to sanity-check `f`.\n.probe_points <- function(domain, x_init) {\n  a <- domain[1]; b <- domain[2]\n  if (!is.null(x_init)) return(x_init)\n  if (is.finite(a) && is.finite(b)) {\n    a + (b - a) * c(0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9)\n  } else if (is.finite(a)) {\n    a + c(0.5, 1, 2, 5)\n  } else if (is.finite(b)) {\n    b - c(0.5, 1, 2, 5)\n  } else {\n    c(-5, -1, 0, 1, 5)\n  }\n}\n\n## -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n## 2. Log-density and numerical derivative\n## -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#' Build a (possibly unnormalized) log-density function from f, clamped to\n#' `domain` so that log(0) outside the support does not propagate as NaN.\n.make_log_density <- function(f, domain) {\n  function(x) {\n    val <- rep(-Inf, length(x))\n    inside <- x > domain[1] & x < domain[2]\n    if (any(inside)) {\n      fx <- f(x[inside])\n      val[inside] <- log(fx)\n    }\n    val\n  }\n}\n\n#' Central-difference numerical derivative of `logf`, clamped to stay\n#' strictly inside `domain` so evaluation never lands outside the support.\n.make_log_density_derivative <- function(logf, domain) {\n  function(x) {\n    eps <- pmax(1e-6, abs(x) * 1e-5)\n    lo <- pmax(x - eps, domain[1] + 1e-10)\n    hi <- pmin(x + eps, domain[2] - 1e-10)\n    h <- pmax(hi - lo, 1e-12)\n    (logf(hi) - logf(lo)) / h\n  }\n}\n\n## -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n## 3. Choosing starting abscissae\n## -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#' Expand `x` outward (in the given direction) until `hprime` has the sign\n#' required for the tail to be integrable, or until the finite domain bound\n#' is reached (in which case no sign condition is required).\n.expand_to_valid_tail <- function(x, hprime, bound, direction, min_slope,\n                                   max_iter = 60) {\n  step <- max(1, abs(x))\n  for (i in seq_len(max_iter)) {\n    slope <- hprime(x)\n    ok <- if (direction > 0) slope <= -min_slope else slope >= min_slope\n    if (ok) return(x)\n    x_next <- x + direction * step\n    if (direction > 0 && x_next >= bound) {\n      if (is.finite(bound)) return(bound - 1e-6 * max(1, abs(bound)))\n    }\n    if (direction < 0 && x_next <= bound) {\n      if (is.finite(bound)) return(bound + 1e-6 * max(1, abs(bound)))\n    }\n    x <- x_next\n    step <- step * 2\n  }\n  stop(\"Could not find a starting point with the required tail behavior \",\n       \"(h'(x) must eventually change sign away from the mode). This \",\n       \"usually means the density is not log-concave, or its tails decay \",\n       \"too slowly.\", call. = FALSE)\n}\n\n#' Choose initial abscissae satisfying the ARS boundary requirements:\n#' h'(x1) > 0 if the domain is unbounded below, h'(xk) < 0 if unbounded\n#' above. Interior guesses are used as-is (and refined by later hull\n#' updates during sampling).\n.initialize_abscissae <- function(hprime, domain, x_init, min_slope = 1e-8) {\n  a <- domain[1]; b <- domain[2]\n\n  if (!is.null(x_init)) {\n    pts <- sort(unique(x_init))\n  } else if (is.finite(a) && is.finite(b)) {\n    pts <- a + (b - a) * c(0.25, 0.75)\n  } else if (is.finite(a)) {\n    pts <- a + c(0.5, 2)\n  } else if (is.finite(b)) {\n    pts <- b - c(2, 0.5)\n  } else {\n    pts <- c(-1, 1)\n  }\n\n  if (!is.finite(a)) {\n    pts[1] <- .expand_to_valid_tail(pts[1], hprime, a, direction = -1,\n                                     min_slope = min_slope)\n  }\n  k <- length(pts)\n  if (!is.finite(b)) {\n    pts[k] <- .expand_to_valid_tail(pts[k], hprime, b, direction = 1,\n                                     min_slope = min_slope)\n  }\n\n  pts <- sort(unique(pts))\n  if (length(pts) < 2) {\n    stop(\"Failed to construct at least 2 distinct starting abscissae; \",\n         \"try supplying `x_init` explicitly.\", call. = FALSE)\n  }\n  pts\n}\n\n## -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n## 4. Building the piecewise-linear upper/lower hulls\n## -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#' Check that h' is non-increasing across sorted abscissae (necessary\n#' condition for h = log f to be concave). Raises an error otherwise.\n.check_log_concavity <- function(absc, hpx, tol) {\n  if (length(absc) < 2) return(invisible(TRUE))\n  d <- diff(hpx)\n  if (any(d > tol)) {\n    bad <- which(d > tol)[1]\n    stop(sprintf(paste0(\n      \"Non-log-concave density detected: the derivative of log(f) \",\n      \"increased between x = %.6g and x = %.6g (h'=%.6g then h'=%.6g). \",\n      \"Adaptive rejection sampling requires a log-concave density.\"),\n      absc[bad], absc[bad + 1], hpx[bad], hpx[bad + 1]), call. = FALSE)\n  }\n  invisible(TRUE)\n}\n\n#' Construct the upper-hull tangent-line intersection points z_1..z_{k-1}\n#' and the domain-bounded piece boundaries. Detects out-of-order\n#' intersections, another symptom of a non-log-concave density.\n.compute_intersections <- function(absc, hx, hpx, domain, tol) {\n  k <- length(absc)\n  if (k == 1) return(numeric(0))\n  z <- numeric(k - 1)\n  for (i in seq_len(k - 1)) {\n    den <- hpx[i] - hpx[i + 1]\n    if (abs(den) < 1e-12) {\n      z[i] <- (absc[i] + absc[i + 1]) / 2\n    } else {\n      num <- (hx[i + 1] - hx[i]) - (absc[i + 1] * hpx[i + 1] - absc[i] * hpx[i])\n      z[i] <- num / den\n    }\n    if (z[i] < absc[i] - tol || z[i] > absc[i + 1] + tol) {\n      stop(sprintf(paste0(\n        \"Non-log-concave density detected: tangent lines at x = %.6g and \",\n        \"x = %.6g intersect out of order (z = %.6g). Adaptive rejection \",\n        \"sampling requires a log-concave density.\"),\n        absc[i], absc[i + 1], z[i]), call. = FALSE)\n    }\n    z[i] <- min(max(z[i], absc[i]), absc[i + 1])\n  }\n  z\n}\n\n#' Build the full hull representation used for sampling: per-piece slope,\n#' intercept, and probability mass (integral of exp(upper hull)).\n.build_hull <- function(absc, hx, hpx, domain, concavity_tol = 1e-3) {\n  .check_log_concavity(absc, hpx, concavity_tol)\n  z <- .compute_intersections(absc, hx, hpx, domain, tol = 1e-6)\n  k <- length(absc)\n  bounds <- c(domain[1], z, domain[2])\n  baseline <- max(hx)\n  const <- hx - baseline # tangent-line intercepts relative to baseline\n\n  min_slope <- 1e-10\n  masses <- numeric(k)\n  for (i in seq_len(k)) {\n    lo <- bounds[i]; hi <- bounds[i + 1]\n    m <- hpx[i]\n    explo <- if (is.infinite(lo)) 0 else exp(const[i] + m * (lo - absc[i]))\n    exphi <- if (is.infinite(hi)) 0 else exp(const[i] + m * (hi - absc[i]))\n    masses[i] <- if (abs(m) < min_slope) {\n      (hi - lo) * exp(const[i])\n    } else {\n      (exphi - explo) / m\n    }\n  }\n\n  list(absc = absc, hx = hx, hpx = hpx, z = z, bounds = bounds,\n       baseline = baseline, const = const, masses = masses, domain = domain)\n}\n\n## -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n## 5. Evaluating the hulls\n## -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#' Evaluate the piecewise-linear upper hull u(x) at a single point x,\n#' given which piece index x falls in.\n.upper_hull_piece <- function(hull, i) {\n  hull$hx[i] + 0 # placeholder for readability; real eval is in .eval_upper\n}\n\n.eval_upper_hull <- function(hull, x) {\n  i <- findInterval(x, hull$bounds, rightmost.closed = TRUE)\n  i <- min(max(i, 1L), length(hull$absc))\n  hull$hx[i] + hull$hpx[i] * (x - hull$absc[i])\n}\n\n#' Evaluate the piecewise-linear lower hull (squeeze) l(x). Returns -Inf\n#' outside the span of the current abscissae, as required by the method.\n.eval_lower_hull <- function(hull, x) {\n  absc <- hull$absc; hx <- hull$hx\n  k <- length(absc)\n  if (x <= absc[1] || x >= absc[k]) return(-Inf)\n  i <- findInterval(x, absc, rightmost.closed = TRUE)\n  i <- min(max(i, 1L), k - 1L)\n  lo <- absc[i]; hi <- absc[i + 1]\n  ((hi - x) * hx[i] + (x - lo) * hx[i + 1]) / (hi - lo)\n}\n\n## -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n## 6. Sampling from the upper hull\n## -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#' Draw one point from the piecewise-exponential upper hull via inverse-CDF\n#' sampling. Returns the draw and the exact upper-hull log-value there\n#' (so callers never need to re-evaluate the upper hull separately).\n.sample_upper_hull <- function(hull) {\n  k <- length(hull$absc)\n  total <- sum(hull$masses)\n  probs <- hull$masses / total\n  piece <- sample.int(k, size = 1, prob = probs)\n\n  lo <- hull$bounds[piece]; hi <- hull$bounds[piece + 1]\n  m <- hull$hpx[piece]; x_i <- hull$absc[piece]; c_i <- hull$const[piece]\n  r <- runif(1)\n\n  min_slope <- 1e-10\n  if (abs(m) < min_slope) {\n    x_star <- lo + r * (hi - lo)\n  } else {\n    explo <- if (is.infinite(lo)) 0 else exp(c_i + m * (lo - x_i))\n    target <- explo + r * m * hull$masses[piece]\n    x_star <- x_i + (log(target) - c_i) / m\n  }\n  u_val <- hull$hx[piece] + hull$hpx[piece] * (x_star - x_i)\n  list(x = x_star, u = u_val)\n}\n\n## -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n## 7. Main driver\n## -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#' Adaptive rejection sampling (Gilks & Wild, 1992).\n#'\n#' @param n Number of samples to draw (positive integer).\n#' @param f A vectorized function computing the (possibly unnormalized)\n#'   density of interest, e.g. \\code{dnorm} or \\code{function(x) exp(-x^2)}.\n#'   \\code{f} must be log-concave on \\code{domain}.\n#' @param domain Length-2 numeric vector \\code{c(lower, upper)} giving the\n#'   support of the density. Defaults to the whole real line.\n#' @param x_init Optional numeric vector (length >= 2) of starting\n#'   abscissae strictly inside \\code{domain}. If omitted, ars() picks its\n#'   own starting points automatically.\n#' @param max_abscissae Safety cap on the number of hull points; exceeding\n#'   it signals a misbehaving density (default 500).\n#' @param max_iter Safety cap on the number of proposal draws (default\n#'   \\code{200 * n + 2000}).\n#' @param concavity_tol Numerical tolerance used when checking that the\n#'   derivative of log(f) is non-increasing (default 1e-3).\n#' @param verbose If TRUE, prints progress information.\n#'\n#' @return A numeric vector of \\code{n} samples, with an attached\n#'   \\code{\"diagnostics\"} attribute listing the number of proposals drawn\n#'   and the final number of abscissae used.\nars <- function(n, f, domain = c(-Inf, Inf), x_init = NULL,\n                 max_abscissae = 500, max_iter = NULL,\n                 concavity_tol = 1e-3, verbose = FALSE) {\n  .validate_ars_inputs(n, f, domain, x_init)\n  n <- as.integer(round(n))\n  if (is.null(max_iter)) max_iter <- 200L * n + 2000L\n\n  logf <- .make_log_density(f, domain)\n  hprime <- .make_log_density_derivative(logf, domain)\n\n  absc <- .initialize_abscissae(hprime, domain, x_init)\n  hx <- logf(absc)\n  hpx <- hprime(absc)\n  if (any(!is.finite(hx))) {\n    stop(\"log(f(x)) is not finite at the starting abscissae; supply \",\n         \"`x_init` points where the density is strictly positive.\",\n         call. = FALSE)\n  }\n  hull <- .build_hull(absc, hx, hpx, domain, concavity_tol)\n\n  samples <- numeric(n)\n  n_accepted <- 0L\n  n_proposals <- 0L\n\n  while (n_accepted < n) {\n    if (n_proposals >= max_iter) {\n      stop(sprintf(paste0(\n        \"Exceeded max_iter = %d proposals after accepting %d/%d samples. \",\n        \"This may indicate the density is not log-concave, or that \",\n        \"`domain` is misspecified.\"), max_iter, n_accepted, n), call. = FALSE)\n    }\n    n_proposals <- n_proposals + 1L\n\n    draw <- .sample_upper_hull(hull)\n    x_star <- draw$x\n    u_star <- draw$u\n    w <- runif(1)\n    l_star <- .eval_lower_hull(hull, x_star)\n\n    if (log(w) <= l_star - u_star) {\n      n_accepted <- n_accepted + 1L\n      samples[n_accepted] <- x_star\n      next\n    }\n\n    hx_star <- logf(x_star)\n    hpx_star <- hprime(x_star)\n\n    if (log(w) <= hx_star - u_star) {\n      n_accepted <- n_accepted + 1L\n      samples[n_accepted] <- x_star\n    }\n\n    absc <- c(hull$absc, x_star)\n    ord <- order(absc)\n    absc <- absc[ord]\n    hx <- c(hull$hx, hx_star)[ord]\n    hpx <- c(hull$hpx, hpx_star)[ord]\n    if (length(absc) > max_abscissae) {\n      stop(sprintf(\n        \"Number of hull abscissae exceeded max_abscissae = %d. This \",\n        \"usually indicates the density is not log-concave.\",\n        max_abscissae), call. = FALSE)\n    }\n    hull <- .build_hull(absc, hx, hpx, domain, concavity_tol)\n\n    if (verbose && n_accepted %% max(1L, n %/% 10L) == 0L) {\n      message(sprintf(\"ars: %d/%d accepted, %d proposals, %d abscissae\",\n                       n_accepted, n, n_proposals, length(absc)))\n    }\n  }\n\n  attr(samples, \"diagnostics\") <- list(\n    n_proposals = n_proposals,\n    n_abscissae_final = length(hull$absc),\n    acceptance_rate = n / n_proposals\n  )\n  samples\n}\n\n## -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n## 8. Test suite\n## -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#' Print one PASS/FAIL line for a distributional test and return whether it\n#' passed.\n.report_distribution_test <- function(name, samples, mean_theo, sd_theo,\n                                       cdf_theo, mean_tol_sd = 5,\n                                       sd_rel_tol = 0.2, ks_alpha = 0.01) {\n  n <- length(samples)\n  mean_hat <- mean(samples)\n  sd_hat <- sd(samples)\n\n  se_mean <- sd_theo / sqrt(n)\n  mean_ok <- abs(mean_hat - mean_theo) <= mean_tol_sd * se_mean\n  sd_ok <- abs(sd_hat - sd_theo) / sd_theo <= sd_rel_tol\n  ks <- suppressWarnings(ks.test(samples, cdf_theo))\n  ks_ok <- ks$p.value >= ks_alpha\n\n  pass <- mean_ok && sd_ok && ks_ok\n  cat(sprintf(\n    \"%s: %s | n=%d mean=%.4f (theoretical=%.4f) sd=%.4f (theoretical=%.4f) KS_p=%.4f\\n\",\n    name, if (pass) \"PASS\" else \"FAIL\", n, mean_hat, mean_theo, sd_hat,\n    sd_theo, ks$p.value))\n  pass\n}\n\n#' Print one PASS/FAIL line for a test that expects ars() to raise an error\n#' (e.g. invalid inputs, or a non-log-concave density).\n.report_error_test <- function(name, expr) {\n  result <- tryCatch({ force(expr); \"no_error\" },\n                      error = function(e) conditionMessage(e))\n  pass <- !identical(result, \"no_error\")\n  msg <- if (pass) result else \"expected an error but none was raised\"\n  cat(sprintf(\"%s: %s | %s\\n\", name, if (pass) \"PASS\" else \"FAIL\", msg))\n  pass\n}\n\n#' Run the full ars() test suite and print PASS/FAIL results for each test.\n#' Also writes sample draws from the normal and exponential tests to\n#' normal_samples.txt and exponential_samples.txt for inspection.\ntest <- function() {\n  set.seed(20240613)\n  results <- logical(0)\n  add <- function(x) results <<- c(results, x)\n\n  cat(\"=======================================================\\n\")\n  cat(\"Adaptive Rejection Sampling (Gilks & Wild, 1992) add(.report_module_tests())\n  cat(\"\\n\")\n\n  writeLines(format(s_norm, digits = 10), \"/app/normal_samples.txt\")\n  writeLines(format(s_exp, digits = 10), \"/app/exponential_samples.txt\")\n
